summary: The strongest predictor of income class is 'marital-status', with permutation importance (mean ROC-AUC drop when shuffled) of 0.0429 on held-out data, followed by capital-gain, education-num, age. This ranking was consistent across 5 independently reseeded train/test splits and model refits.
primary_metric_name: top feature permutation importance (mean ROC-AUC drop)
methodological_choices: Dropped redundant 'education' string column (kept 'education-num'). Missing categorical values ('?') kept as explicit 'Missing' category rather than imputed or dropped. One-hot encoding for categoricals, passthrough for numerics. Primary model: RandomForestClassifier (300 trees, min_samples_leaf=2, class_weight='balanced' for the ~3:1 <=50K/>50K imbalance), compared against a LogisticRegression baseline (RF test ROC-AUC=0.9178, LogReg test ROC-AUC=0.9063). Importance method: permutation importance (10 repeats) on a 30% held-out stratified test set, chosen over impurity-based importance because impurity importance is biased toward high-cardinality categorical features; impurity-based importances were also computed and aggregated per original column for reference and agreed on the top feature ('marital-status').
verification_method: Recomputed permutation importance under 5 independent reseeded train/test splits (random_state 1-5, fresh 70/30 split and model refit each time, 5 repeats each), and additionally ran 5-fold stratified cross-validated ROC-AUC for the primary model.
verification_result: Top feature ('marital-status') was ranked #1 in all 5 reseeded runs (consistent=True). Its permutation importance ranged 0.0429-0.0452 across the 6 total runs (original + 5 reseeds), mean 0.0437. 5-fold CV ROC-AUC for the primary model: 0.9185 +/- 0.0016 (fold scores: [np.float64(0.9156), np.float64(0.9194), np.float64(0.9178), np.float64(0.9199), np.float64(0.9197)]). Finding held up.
